name: Minnesota Eats: Restaurants
subtitle: Juicy Lucys & Supper Clubs
description:
Minnesota's restaurants, from the two Minneapolis bars that both claim the Juicy Lucy to smoked Lake Superior fish up the North Shore.

Minnesota Eats is a free guide to eating in Minnesota: 5 Juicy Lucy bars, 4 supper clubs and walleye spots, 8 Hmong and Southeast Asian kitchens, 5 Somali and East African kitchens, 11 North Shore and Iron Range stops and 15 classic counters and icons we checked by hand, plus 10,238 restaurants, cafés, bars and bakeries in 711 towns, from Minneapolis and St. Paul to Duluth, Rochester and St. Cloud. No account, no ads.

MINNESOTA GUIDES
• Juicy Lucys: the cheese-stuffed burger, with both claimants, Matt's Bar and the 5-8 Club.
• Walleye & Supper Clubs: lake-country supper clubs and walleye.
• Hmong & Southeast Asian: St. Paul's Hmong markets and University Avenue kitchens.
• Somali & East African: Afro Deli, Deg Deg Grill and more in the Twin Cities.
• North Shore & Iron Range: smoked fish, pie, potica and pasties.
• Classic Counters & Icons: diners, delis and long-running favorites.
• Oldest Places: 5 places open at their address since 1960 or earlier.
• James Beard Honors: 22 honored Minnesota restaurants.

FIND IT FAST
• Sort by distance, or browse the map by guide.
• Search by name, town, street or dish: "juicy lucy", "supper club", "potica".
• Filter by town or cuisine, or hide chains.
• Save places, and find hand-checked places from iPhone search (Spotlight).

LIVE DETAILS FROM APPLE MAPS
Tap "Ratings, hours & photos" on any place to open Apple Maps' own place card, with current hours, photos, ratings and directions.

HOW THE LISTS ARE BUILT
Every guide place was checked by hand in fall 2026 against a dated 2025 or 2026 article or a visitor bureau's own page. The rest come from Overture Maps open data, kept by the reliability rule we tested against the City of Minneapolis's own restaurant list. Only Minneapolis publishes its inspections as open data, so 914 Minneapolis places show the City's own latest score, as the City publishes it; the app computes no grades, and places elsewhere link to the state health department's page on who inspects where. Website links are checked too. Nothing is ranked by star ratings or inspections. Newer restaurant data downloads from the Minnesota Eats website when there is some.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no tracking, no ads. Your location, if you share it, only sorts lists on your device. Saved places stay on your device.

Places open and close, so check before you go. Spot a mistake? Email nick@eatsranked.com.

An independent app, not affiliated with any restaurant, chain or government agency (including the State of Minnesota, the Minnesota Department of Health or the City of Minneapolis), any visitor bureau, the Minnesota Vikings, or the James Beard Foundation. James Beard Foundation and James Beard Award are trademarks of the James Beard Foundation. Place data from Overture Maps Foundation (CDLA Permissive 2.0) and others; sources and licenses are on the About tab.

reviewNotes:
1. Purpose and audience: Minnesota Eats is a free guide to restaurants in Minnesota (the U.S. state). Its focus is the state's own food: Juicy Lucys, supper clubs and walleye, Hmong and Southeast Asian kitchens, Somali and East African kitchens, the North Shore and the Iron Range, and classic counters, 50 places checked by hand in fall 2026 against a 2025 or 2026 source, plus the James Beard honorees. It also lists 10,238 restaurants, cafés and bars in 711 towns from open map data. It is for residents and visitors deciding where to eat, with no ads, account or tracking.

2. How to use it (no login, no setup, no sample files needed):
- Home → Juicy Lucys (or Walleye & Supper Clubs, Hmong & Southeast Asian, Somali & East African, North Shore & Iron Range, Classic Counters & Icons, James Beard Honors, Oldest Places, Near Me) → tap any place.
- On a place, tap "Ratings, hours & photos" to open Apple Maps' own place card through MapKit. Directions, Call and Website are below it. Minneapolis places show the City of Minneapolis's latest published inspection score with a link to the City's page; places elsewhere link to the Minnesota Department of Health's page on who inspects where.
- Search from the Home search box by name, town, street or dish ("juicy lucy", "supper club", "potica").
- The Map tab shows each guide as pins. "My location" and the Nearest sort use location only if allowed, on the device.
- The heart saves a place on the device (Saved tab). The About tab lists the sources, licenses and the independence statement.
- On iPad, a sidebar replaces the tabs; a place opens in the right-hand column.
- Location: if you're outside Minnesota (as App Review usually is), the map says so and stays on Minnesota, and distance sorting still works from where you are.
- "Minnesota Eats" is the Home Screen name of "Minnesota Eats: Restaurants".

3. External services and data:
- Apple MapKit: maps, local search to find a place's Apple Maps listing, and Apple's place card for live hours, photos and ratings.
- Core Location: optional, on-device only, for distance sorting.
- Data updates: at most once a day, the app checks the Minnesota Eats website (static files on GitHub Pages) for newer restaurant data and downloads it if there is some. The requests carry no identifiers or location.
- No backend, accounts, analytics, advertising, payments or AI services. The restaurant data is bundled in the app.
- Bundled data sources: Overture Maps Foundation open place data (CDLA Permissive 2.0 and others; license texts are in the app); the City of Minneapolis's open food-inspection and on-sale liquor data (the City has waived copyright); James Beard Foundation honors (facts only); and our own research of public websites, local news and visitor-bureau pages.
- The website with the privacy policy and support page is static and hosted on GitHub Pages: https://nickstrom5.github.io/minnesota-eats/

4. Regional differences: none. The content covers Minnesota; the app is offered in the United States and works the same everywhere.

5. Regulated or protected material: the app is not in a regulated industry and includes no protected third-party material. The data is open-licensed or public record, with attribution in the app.
